title: The actuator question: CNO vs. DCZ
objective: Explain why CNO is not truly inert, and why many labs now use deschloroclozapine (DCZ) or careful CNO controls.

steps.title: The drug was supposed to be inert
steps.body: The original [[DREADD]] [[actuator]], **[[CNO|clozapine-N-oxide]] (CNO)**, was chosen because it was thought to be biologically inert — no effect except through the DREADD. For years that assumption went mostly unchallenged.

steps.title: The catch: CNO converts back to clozapine
steps.body: A key finding: **CNO is reverse-metabolized to [[clozapine]]** in the body. Clozapine readily crosses the blood–brain barrier and binds many endogenous receptors. Work from Michael Michaelides and colleagues argued that clozapine — not CNO itself — is the molecule that actually reaches and activates the DREADD, and that it can cause **off-target behavioral effects on its own**.

flag.note: The magnitude of the CNO/clozapine confound depends on dose and species; the fix (controls + better actuators) is widely accepted.

visual.alt: CNO back-converts to clozapine, which crosses the blood-brain barrier and binds off-target neurons, producing an effect not caused by the DREADD.
visual.caption: CNO → clozapine → crosses the BBB → off-target effect.

steps.prompt: Why does the CNO→clozapine conversion threaten an experiment?
options: Clozapine is inert, so it only dilutes the effective dose of CNO
Clozapine has its own CNS effects, so a drug-only change may mislead
The conversion makes the DREADD receptor itself stop working
It matters only in cell culture, never in a living animal
steps.explanation: If the actuator itself alters behavior, you can't cleanly attribute an effect to your neurons. That's exactly why a DREADD-free + actuator control is essential (next lesson).

variants.setup: CNO can back-convert to clozapine in the body.
variants.prompt: Why does that threaten a DREADD experiment?
options: Clozapine is inert, so it only dilutes the effective dose of CNO
Clozapine has its own CNS effects, so a drug-only change may mislead
The conversion makes the DREADD receptor itself stop working
It matters only in cell culture, never in a living animal
variants.reveal: If the actuator itself alters the brain, you can't attribute an effect to your neurons without a DREADD-free control.

steps.title: Two fixes
steps.body:
**1) Control for the drug.** Give the same actuator to DREADD-free animals; any effect there is the drug's own.

**2) Use a better actuator.** **Deschloroclozapine ([[DCZ]])** is more potent and selective for DREADDs, works at much lower doses, and has less off-target activity than CNO — reducing (not eliminating) the confound. Many labs have moved to DCZ or to low-dose CNO with strict controls.

steps.scenario: A labmate reports a strong behavioral change after giving a high dose of CNO to their [[hM4Di]] mice. They have no DREADD-free group.
steps.prompt: What is the most important gap?
options: They forgot to measure the animals' core body temperature
No DREADD-free + CNO group, so the effect could be the drug
CNO is completely unable to activate the hM4Di receptor
They should simply have used a much larger number of mice
steps.explanation: High-dose CNO maximizes back-conversion to clozapine. The missing control is the one that would rule out a drug-only explanation. Lower dose, DCZ, and the right controls all address this.
steps.followUp: How would you redesign it? (Add DREADD-free + actuator controls; switch to DCZ at a low validated dose; include a DREADD+ vehicle group.)

steps.setup: You run DREADD-free mice and give them the actuator alone. You see a measurable change in your behavioral readout.
options: Your neurons must clearly have caused the observed effect
The actuator has its own effect, so the result is confounded
The DREADD is working exactly as intended in this case
steps.reveal: A signal in the DREADD-free + actuator group is the actuator's own footprint. You must subtract/account for it — or lower the dose / switch actuator — before claiming your neurons did anything.

variants.prompt: In a DREADD-free group, the actuator alone produces the same behavioral change. What does that tell you?
options: Your neurons must clearly have caused the observed effect
The actuator has its own effect, so the result is confounded
The DREADD is working exactly as intended in this case
variants.explanation: An actuator-alone effect means you can't credit your neurons until you account for it.
